Finding the right mobile carrier depends mostly on where you spend your time and how much data you use, but here are a few of the best options broken down by category.

If you’re prioritizing reliability and coverage above all else, **Verizon** is typically the gold standard, particularly in rural or remote areas. **AT&T** is also excellent with very broad 5G coverage, and both tend to have the highest prices.

For a balance of price and performance, **T-Mobile** is a great pick. They have a massive 5G footprint in urban areas and usually offer more data for less money than the "Big Three" legacy carriers. If you live in a city, T-Mobile is hard to beat.

If you want to save a lot of money, consider a "Mobile Virtual Network Operator" (MVNO). **Mint Mobile** (runs on T-Mobile) and **Visible** (runs on Verizon) offer premium data at a fraction of the price, though you might experience slightly lower priority during peak congestion.

If you are an international traveler or need a lot of hotspot data, **Google Fi** (using T-Mobile and USCC) is excellent because of its flexible plans and international roaming, though it can be pricier for heavy domestic users.

Quick questions to narrow it down:
*   Are you in a major city or a rural area?
*   Are you looking for a family plan, or just one line?
*   Do you need a lot of high-speed data, or mostly talk/text?
